summary: Folke Bergman worked in archaeology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Uppsala University (~1922–1927) and served as Amanuens of East Asian collections at the Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities (~1935–1946).

An indologist and Central Asian scholar, Falconer studied at Marischal College, Aberdeen, and under Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, and Heinrich Ewald. In 1834, he became Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindustani at University College London.

Forster Fitzgerald Arbuthnot was an indologist who studied at the East India Company College in 1851. He served in the Indian Civil Service as Collector of Bombay City and Island (1853–1878) and founded the Kama Shastra Society.

Frances Wood is a scholar of sinology, archaeology, and Central Asian studies. She studied at Newnham College, Cambridge, and Peking University, later working at the British Library (~1977–2013) and as a Clinical Psychologist at North Bristol NHS Trust (2023).
Francesca Fremantle is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1967–1971) and under Chögyam Trungpa (~1971–1987).

Francesca Tarocco is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS (2005) and held positions as Professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (2016) and Visiting Associate Professor at NYU Shanghai (2017).

Francesco Adolfo Cannizzaro worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indian studies. He earned a law degree from the University of Catania in 1894 and studied under Angelo De Gubernatis between ~1891 and 1893.

Francesco Cimmino was an indologist who studied at the University of Naples under Michele Kerbaker and at Turin under Giovanni Flechia. He taught at Liceo Antonio Genovesi and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Naples from 1914 to 1935.

Francesco Lorenzo Pullè was an indologist and linguist who studied under Angelo De Gubernatis, Albrecht Weber, Theodor Mommsen, and Heinrich Kiepert. He was a professor at the University of Padua (1875–1889) and the University of Bologna (1899–1925).

Francesco Ribezzo was a linguist and archaeologist who studied at Naples under Michele Kerbaker, at Leipzig, and under Alfredo Trombetti. He taught at Naples (1914–1921), the University of Messina (1921–1925), and the University of Palermo (1925–1948).

Francesco Scerbo was an indologist and linguist who studied at Seminario Vescovile di Nicastro and under Angelo De Gubernatis and Antelmo Severini. He taught Hebrew at the University of Florence as libero docente (1892) and incaricato (1903–1924).

Francesco Sferra is an indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Raffaele Torella. He held posts as professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2000–~2005) and was attested as professor at Naples Federico II (2010–2016).

Francis A. Wood was a linguist who studied at Northwestern, Göttingen, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1895). He was Professor of German at Cornell College (1897–1903) and Assistant Professor at the University of Chicago (1903–1927).

Francis Balfour was an indologist who completed his medical degree at the University of Edinburgh in 1767. He served in the East India Company as an Assistant Surgeon starting in 1769 and as a full surgeon from 1777 to 1807.

Francis Brandt was an indologist and linguist who studied at Brasenose College, Oxford (~1858–1870). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1890) and lectured in Tamil and Indian Law at the University of Cambridge (1891–1895).
Francis Brinkley worked in the field of Japanology. He was educated at the Royal School Dungannon and held a post at the University of Tokyo from ~1878 to 1881.

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh under John Hope. He served in the Bengal Medical Service (1794–1815), directed the Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815), and became Keeper of the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh in 1815.

Francis Gladwin was an indologist and Iranian studies scholar. A co-founder and member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1812), he was appointed as the first Professor of Persian at Fort William College in 1801.

Francis Harold Cook was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as Professor at UC Riverside (~1970–1989) and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 1999.
Francis John Monahan was an indologist and historian who studied at Balliol College, Oxford, in 1883. He served as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service beginning in 1885.
